runs.notes: HQ headline + Richardson medium (h=0.5). 1 GPU. Metrics-only. Raised 1 -> 3 GPUs on 2026-08-19 after the single- and dual-card attempts failed the same way: the mesh keeps refining, so speed decays (22 -> 2.3 units/h by t=44) while per-card memory grows ~6 GB/h, and attempt 1 OOMed. Splitting the domain across 3 ranks cuts the per-card footprint by about a third and moves the ceiling out past t=64. Compute layout only - physics_frozen untouched.

Richardson coarse (h=0.667). 1 GPU. Window cut 64 -> 32 on 2026-08-20. The headline transport curve plateaus at t~43-45 (0.508 at 43, 0.510 at 48), so everything past ~45 was cost with no signal, and it is exactly where memory triples (51 GB of data at t=24, 92 GB at t=42, 152 GB at t=48). At t=32 a cell needs ~58 GB and fits one card, which is what makes this matrix runnable. The convergence claim compares rungs against each other, so the absolute value of the truncated window does not matter; the headline number is quoted from the separate t=51 RM run instead.

Richardson intermediate rung (h=0.533). Replaces the retired N=384 fine rung (OOMs on one GPU; ladder capped per GPU_RUN_PLAN.md 2).
